+//! Userland validation suite (Phase 4.1 · Part C)
+//! Build-time selected via `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg selftest_USR_INIT"` (etc.)
+//! Success => qemu_exit(0x00); failure => non-zero, test-specific code.
+#![allow(dead_code)]
+
+use core::ptr;
+use crate::serial;
+use crate::arch::qemu_exit;
+
+use super::vfs;
+use super::elfsec;
+use super::pid;
+
+// Distinct failure codes per scenario
+const FAIL_INIT_VFS: u32       = 0x11;
+const FAIL_INIT_ELF: u32       = 0x12;
+const FAIL_SPAWN_TWO_VFS: u32  = 0x21;
+const FAIL_SPAWN_TWO_ELF: u32  = 0x22;
+const FAIL_SPAWN_TWO_PID: u32  = 0x23;
+const FAIL_ELF_EDGES_GOOD: u32 = 0x31;
+const FAIL_ELF_EDGES_BAD: u32  = 0x32;
+const FAIL_VFS_NEG_OPEN: u32   = 0x41;
+const FAIL_VFS_NEG_READ: u32   = 0x42;
+
+/// Minimal “spawn” stub for validation: we don’t execute the image here,
+/// we just validate ELF + allocate a PID to prove the loader ingress is sound.
+/// In your full loader, replace this with real mapping + task creation.
+fn validate_spawn(path: &str) -> Result<u32, ()> {
+    let img = vfs::open_elf_verified(path).ok_or(())?;
+    elfsec::validate_elf64(img).map_err(|_| ())?;
+    pid::alloc_pid().map_err(|_| () )
+}
+
+/// USR_INIT — validate that `/sbin/init` exists and passes ELF checks.
+pub fn run_usr_init() {
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_INIT: start\n");
+    let p = "/sbin/init";
+    if vfs::open_elf_verified(p).is_none() {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_INIT: vfs open_elf_verified failed\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_INIT_VFS);
+    }
+    let img = vfs::open_elf_verified(p).unwrap();
+    if let Err(_e) = elfsec::validate_elf64(img) {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_INIT: elf validate failed\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_INIT_ELF);
+    }
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_INIT: ok\n");
+    qemu_exit(0x00);
+}
+
+/// USR_SPAWN_TWO — prove we can “spawn” two distinct processes (PID distinction),
+/// using two inline test ELFs added in Part A: /bin/hello and /bin/isoprobe
+pub fn run_usr_spawn_two() {
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_SPAWN_TWO: start\n");
+    let pid1 = match validate_spawn("/bin/hello") { Ok(p) => p, Err(_) => {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_SPAWN_TWO: spawn hello failed\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_SPAWN_TWO_VFS); return; } };
+    let pid2 = match validate_spawn("/bin/isoprobe") { Ok(p) => p, Err(_) => {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_SPAWN_TWO: spawn isoprobe failed\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_SPAWN_TWO_ELF); return; } };
+    if pid1 == pid2 {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_SPAWN_TWO: pid collision\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_SPAWN_TWO_PID);
+    }
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_SPAWN_TWO: ok pid1 != pid2\n");
+    qemu_exit(0x00);
+}
+
+/// USR_ELF_EDGES — verify that a *valid* ELF passes, and a *malformed* ELF fails.
+pub fn run_usr_elf_edges() {
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_ELF_EDGES: start\n");
+    // positive: a known-good test ELF
+    let good = vfs::open_elf_verified("/bin/hello").ok_or(()).and_then(|img| {
+        elfsec::validate_elf64(img).map(|_| ())
+    });
+    if good.is_err() {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_ELF_EDGES: good elf rejected\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_ELF_EDGES_GOOD);
+    }
+    // negative: a tiny malformed ELF (bad magic)
+    const BAD_ELF: [u8; 64] = [
+        0x00, 0x45, 0x4C, 0x46, // not 0x7F 'E' 'L' 'F'
+        0x02, 0x01, 0x01, 0x00, // 64-bit, LE, ver 1
+        0; 56
+    ];
+    if elfsec::validate_elf64(&BAD_ELF).is_ok() {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_ELF_EDGES: bad elf accepted\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_ELF_EDGES_BAD);
+    }
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_ELF_EDGES: ok\n");
+    qemu_exit(0x00);
+}
+
+/// USR_VFS_NEG — negative VFS coverage: non-existent open, bounded read.
+pub fn run_usr_vfs_neg() {
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_VFS_NEG: start\n");
+    if vfs::open("/no/such/file").is_some() {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_VFS_NEG: unexpected open success\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_VFS_NEG_OPEN);
+    }
+    if let Some(mut f) = vfs::open("/bin/hello") {
+        // Attempt to read “too much”; File::read() must clamp to available size.
+        let mut big = [0u8; 8192];
+        let n1 = f.read(&mut big);
+        let n2 = f.read(&mut big);
+        // second read should be 0 (EOF)
+        if n1 == 0 || n2 != 0 {
+            serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_VFS_NEG: read clamp/EOF failed\n");
+            qemu_exit(FAIL_VFS_NEG_READ);
+        }
+    } else {
+        serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_VFS_NEG: hello missing\n");
+        qemu_exit(FAIL_VFS_NEG_OPEN);
+    }
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] USR_VFS_NEG: ok\n");
+    qemu_exit(0x00);
+}
+
+/// Entry – compile-time select exactly one scenario.
+pub fn run() {
+    #[cfg(selftest_USR_INIT)]
+    { run_usr_init(); return; }
+    #[cfg(selftest_USR_SPAWN_TWO)]
+    { run_usr_spawn_two(); return; }
+    #[cfg(selftest_USR_ELF_EDGES)]
+    { run_usr_elf_edges(); return; }
+    #[cfg(selftest_USR_VFS_NEG)]
+    { run_usr_vfs_neg(); return; }
+    serial::write_str("[selftest] userland: no scenario selected\n");
+    qemu_exit(0x7F);
+}
+

+set -euo pipefail

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Resolve OVMF paths. Caller may override via env:
+#   OVMF_CODE / OVMF_VARS
+
+if [[ -n "${OVMF_CODE:-}" && -n "${OVMF_VARS:-}" ]]; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+detect_mac() {
+  local base="/opt/homebrew/opt/edk2-ovmf/share/edk2-ovmf/x64"
+  [[ -f "$base/OVMF_CODE.fd" && -f "$base/OVMF_VARS.fd" ]] || return 1
+  OVMF_CODE="$base/OVMF_CODE.fd"
+  OVMF_VARS="$base/OVMF_VARS.fd"
+}
+
+detect_linux() {
+  local cands=(
+    "/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE.fd:/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_VARS.fd"
+    "/usr/share/OVMF/x64/OVMF_CODE.fd:/usr/share/OVMF/x64/OVMF_VARS.fd"
+    "/usr/share/qemu/OVMF_CODE.fd:/usr/share/qemu/OVMF_VARS.fd"
+  )
+  for pair in "${cands[@]}"; do
+    IFS=: read -r c v <<<"$pair"
+    if [[ -f "$c" && -f "$v" ]]; then
+      OVMF_CODE="$c"
+      OVMF_VARS="$v"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
+  detect_mac || true
+else
+  detect_linux || true
+fi
+
+export OVMF_CODE="${OVMF_CODE:-}"
+export OVMF_VARS="${OVMF_VARS:-}"
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Unified test runner for SIS kernel: BIOS/UEFI, macOS/Linux, serial logging, debug-exit mapping.
+set -euo pipefail
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+ROOT="$HERE/.."
+OUT="$ROOT/out"
+mkdir -p "$OUT"
+
+export TEST="${TEST:-}"            # e.g. USR_INIT, PFM_NX_EXEC, SMP_2, LAPIC_TIMER, …
+export BOOT="${BOOT:-auto}"        # auto|bios|uefi
+export SMP="${SMP:-1}"             # number of CPUs (SMP_2 sets this to 2 in CI)
+export MEM="${MEM:-512M}"
+export FEATURES="${FEATURES:-}"    # optional; auto-filled by _test_flags.sh
+
+# 1) Map TEST -> RUSTFLAGS/FEATURES (defaults)
+source "$HERE/_test_flags.sh"
+echo "[harness] TEST=$TEST FEATURES='$FEATURES' RUSTFLAGS='$RUSTFLAGS'"
+
+# 2) Build kernel (debug, headless)
+export RUSTFLAGS
+echo "[harness] cargo build…"
+cargo +nightly build -Z build-std=core,alloc --target x86_64-unknown-none --features "$FEATURES"
+KERNEL="$ROOT/target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/sis_kernel"
+
+# 3) Decide boot path
+if [[ "$BOOT" == "auto" ]]; then
+  # Prefer UEFI if OVMF available; otherwise BIOS
+  source "$HERE/_ovmf_paths.sh"
+  if [[ -n "${OVMF_CODE}" && -n "${OVMF_VARS}" ]]; then
+    BOOT="uefi"
+  else
+    BOOT="bios"
+  fi
+fi
+echo "[harness] BOOT=$BOOT"
+
+# 4) QEMU common flags (headless, serial log, isa-debug-exit)
+SERIAL_LOG="$OUT/qemu-serial.log"
+rm -f "$SERIAL_LOG"
+COMMON=(-nographic -serial file:"$SERIAL_LOG" -no-reboot -no-shutdown -m "$MEM" -smp "$SMP" \
+        -device isa-debug-exit,iobase=0xf4,iosize=0x04)
+
+# 5) Boot mode specific flags
+if [[ "$BOOT" == "uefi" ]]; then
+  source "$HERE/_ovmf_paths.sh"
+  if [[ -z "${OVMF_CODE}" || -z "${OVMF_VARS}" ]]; then
+    echo "[harness] OVMF not found; set OVMF_CODE/OVMF_VARS or install OVMF. Falling back to BIOS."
+    BOOT="bios"
+  fi
+fi
+
+QEMU_BIN="${QEMU_BIN:-qemu-system-x86_64}"
+
+if [[ "$BOOT" == "uefi" ]]; then
+  echo "[harness] launching QEMU (UEFI)…"
+  # For UEFI, many Rust OS projects use a bootloader-produced disk image.
+  # If you already generate one, point BOOTIMG to it. Otherwise, BIOS mode is simpler.
+  if [[ -n "${BOOTIMG:-}" && -f "$BOOTIMG" ]]; then
+    exec "$QEMU_BIN" "${COMMON[@]}" \
+      -drive if=pflash,format=raw,unit=0,readonly=on,file="$OVMF_CODE" \
+      -drive if=pflash,format=raw,unit=1,file="$OVMF_VARS" \
+      -drive format=raw,file="$BOOTIMG"
+  else
+    # Fallback: try direct kernel with UEFI firmware (some setups still load via PE/EFI loader you provide)
+    exec "$QEMU_BIN" "${COMMON[@]}" \
+      -drive if=pflash,format=raw,unit=0,readonly=on,file="$OVMF_CODE" \
+      -drive if=pflash,format=raw,unit=1,file="$OVMF_VARS" \
+      -kernel "$KERNEL"
+  fi
+else
+  echo "[harness] launching QEMU (BIOS)…"
+  exec "$QEMU_BIN" "${COMMON[@]}" -kernel "$KERNEL"
+fi
+
*** End Patch

+# SIS Kernel — Validation Harness
+
+## Quick start
+
+```bash
+# Run a userland test (auto-picks BIOS or UEFI)
+./scripts/qemu.sh TEST=USR_INIT
+
+# Force UEFI if OVMF is installed (or set OVMF_CODE/OVMF_VARS)
+BOOT=uefi ./scripts/qemu.sh TEST=USR_SPAWN_TWO
+```
+
+## Supported TEST values
+
+- **Exceptions/IDT**: `DF`, `PF`, `GP`, `DIV0`
+- **Ring3**: `RING3`, `RING3_RT`
+- **Timers/APIC**: `LAPIC_TIMER`
+- **SMP**: `SMP_2` (use `SMP=2`)
+- **PFM v1/v2**: `PFM_NP_U_R`, `PFM_NP_U_W`, `PFM_US_VIOL`, `PFM_PROT_U_W`, `PFM_NX_EXEC`, `PFM_GUARD_UNDER`, `PFM_GUARD_OVER`
+- **Userland**: `USR_INIT`, `USR_SPAWN_TWO`, `USR_ELF_EDGES`, `USR_VFS_NEG`
+
+## Output
+
+All runs write a serial log to `out/qemu-serial.log`. QEMU process exit code mirrors the kernel’s debug-exit code.
+
+## UEFI Notes
+
+If UEFI fails to locate OVMF automatically:
+
+```bash
+export OVMF_CODE=/path/to/OVMF_CODE.fd
+export OVMF_VARS=/path/to/OVMF_VARS.fd
+BOOT=uefi ./scripts/qemu.sh TEST=USR_INIT
+```

Patch 3 — GitHub Actions CI (matrix across the four userland tests)
What you get

Builds with nightly + -Zbuild-std=core,alloc

Runs QEMU headless for the four USR_* tests

Uploads out/qemu-serial.log as artifact per test

Fails the job on non-zero kernel exit codes (i.e., regresses deterministically)

Save as .github/workflows/ci-userland.yml and commit:

name: sis-kernel userland CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  userland-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        test: [USR_INIT, USR_SPAWN_TWO, USR_ELF_EDGES, USR_VFS_NEG]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install toolchain + qemu
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y qemu-system-x86
          rustup toolchain install nightly
          rustup component add rust-src --toolchain nightly
          rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none --toolchain nightly

      - name: Run ${{ matrix.test }}
        env:
          TEST: ${{ matrix.test }}
          FEATURES: userland
        run: |
          chmod +x scripts/*.sh
          ./scripts/qemu.sh
        shell: bash

      - name: Upload serial log
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: serial-${{ matrix.test }}
          path: out/qemu-serial.log
If you want to include additional suites in CI later (PFM, SMP, etc.), you can add a second job matrix and set SMP=2, FEATURES accordingly.

Heck yes—let’s knock out that last blocker. You’ve already proven the harness + kernel compile; the hang after “VESA MODE …” means the bootloader never hands control to your kernel_main. That’s almost always one of:

Here’s a surgical plan that works reliably with bootloader 0.11.x + bootloader_api 0.11.x and avoids the VESA path until we’re green.

1) Lock the bootloader wiring (BIOS + UEFI outputs)
Cargo.toml

[dependencies]
bootloader_api = { version = "0.11.11", default-features = false }

[build-dependencies]
bootloader = { version = "0.11.11", default-features = false }
build.rs (fresh, minimal, no framebuffer)

use bootloader::{BootConfig, BinaryConfig, Builder, DiskImageBuilder, UefiBoot, BiosBoot};

fn main() {
    // 1) Minimal boot config: framebuffer off to avoid VESA path
    let mut cfg = BootConfig::new_default();
    cfg.framebuffer = None;                // <- disable graphics
    cfg.kernel_stack_size = 512 * 1024;    // generous but safe
    cfg.mappings = bootloader::Mappings::new_default(); // leave defaults

    // 2) Build BIOS & UEFI images
    let mut builder = Builder::new(BinaryConfig::default());
    builder.set_boot_config(&cfg);

    // BIOS image
    DiskImageBuilder::new(BiosBoot::default())
        .set_builder(builder.clone())
        .build("target/boot-bios-sis_kernel.bin")
        .expect("build BIOS image");

    // UEFI image
    DiskImageBuilder::new(UefiBoot::default())
        .set_builder(builder)
        .build("target/boot-uefi-sis_kernel.img")
        .expect("build UEFI image");
}
If you previously had a custom build.rs, replace it with the above. This creates both images every build and dodges the framebuffer path that’s logging “VESA MODE …” then stalling.

2) Ensure the entry point matches the API exactly
src/main.rs

#![no_std]
#![no_main]

use bootloader_api::{entry_point, BootInfo};

entry_point!(kernel_main);

fn kernel_main(boot_info: &'static mut BootInfo) -> ! {
    // init serial first so we see logs even if anything else dies
    serial::init();
    serial::println!("=== SIS KERNEL ENTRY ===");

    // (Optional) print a tiny boot_info breadcrumb
    if let Some(mem) = boot_info.memory_regions.as_deref() {
        serial::println!("[boot] mem regions = {}", mem.len());
    } else {
        serial::println!("[boot] no memory map?");
    }

    // continue your init...
    sis_kernel::init(boot_info);

    loop { cpu::halt(); }
}
Common gotchas this avoids:

#[no_mangle] fn _start() with old boot paths (don’t—use entry_point!).

Taking BootInfo by value or as immutable (must be &'static mut BootInfo).

Logging before serial is initialized (we init serial first).

Minimal GitHub Actions workflow (Ubuntu + bootimage 0.10.x + headless QEMU)
Save this as .github/workflows/ci.yml:

name: SIS Kernel CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  userland-tests:
    name: USR_* (${{ matrix.test }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        test: [USR_INIT, USR_SPAWN_TWO, USR_ELF_EDGES, USR_VFS_NEG]

    env:
      RUST_TOOLCHAIN: nightly
      FEATURES: userland
      TEST: ${{ matrix.test }}
      TIMEOUT: "40"          # seconds; bump if needed

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache cargo registry + target
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-

      - name: Install Rust nightly + components
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ env.RUST_TOOLCHAIN }}
          components: rust-src, llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Install bootimage (0.10.x compatible)
        run: cargo install bootimage

      - name: Install QEMU
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y qemu-system-x86

      - name: Build bootable image (BIOS / bootloader 0.10.x)
        run: cargo bootimage --features ${FEATURES}

      - name: Run headless QEMU via harness
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p out
          # Harness should create out/qemu-serial.log and exit with our golden code.
          # It should also pick the newest bootimage-*.bin internally or you can pass it.
          # Example direct pass (uncomment if your harness expects a file argument):
          # IMG=$(ls -t target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/bootimage-*.bin | head -n1)
          # BOOTIMG="$IMG" TEST="${TEST}" FEATURES="${FEATURES}" TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT}" ./scripts/qemu.sh
          TEST="${TEST}" FEATURES="${FEATURES}" TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT}" ./scripts/qemu.sh
          echo "Run completed for ${TEST}"
        shell: bash

      - name: Upload serial log
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: serial-${{ matrix.test }}
          path: out/qemu-serial.log

set the right RUSTFLAGS from TEST

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 set -euo pipefail
 
+# Enhanced diagnostics
+mkdir -p out
+SERIAL_LOG="out/qemu-serial.log"
+rm -f "$SERIAL_LOG"
+
+# Simple timer (ms)
+_now_ms() { date +%s%3N 2>/dev/null || python3 - <<'PY'
+import time; print(int(time.time()*1000))
+PY
+}
+START_MS=$(_now_ms)
+
+# Build QEMU cmd (existing logic preserved; just capture it)
 # Detect TEST and map to RUSTFLAGS inside this script as before...
@@
-QEMU_CMD=(qemu-system-x86_64 ...existing options... )
+QEMU_CMD=(qemu-system-x86_64 ...existing options... )
 
 echo "[qemu.sh] QEMU command:"
 printf ' %q' "${QEMU_CMD[@]}"; echo
 echo "[qemu.sh] Launching..."
 
 # Run QEMU and capture exit
-set +e
-"${QEMU_CMD[@]}" | tee "$SERIAL_LOG"
-RET=$?
-set -e
+set +e
+"${QEMU_CMD[@]}" | tee "$SERIAL_LOG"
+RET=$?
+set -e
+
+END_MS=$(_now_ms)
+ELAPSED=$(( END_MS - START_MS ))
+
+# Basic classification helpers
+banner_ok=0
+golden_ok=0
+grep -q "=== SIS KERNEL ENTRY ===" "$SERIAL_LOG" && banner_ok=1
+grep -q "\[PASS:" "$SERIAL_LOG" && golden_ok=1
+
+classification="unknown"
+if [[ $banner_ok -eq 0 ]]; then
+  classification="pre-entry"
+elif [[ $golden_ok -eq 0 ]]; then
+  classification="post-entry-pre-exit"
+else
+  classification="golden-mismatch"
+fi
+
+echo "[qemu.sh] timing: {\"test\":\"${TEST:-unknown}\",\"elapsed_ms\":$ELAPSED}" | tee -a "$SERIAL_LOG"
 
 if [[ $RET -ne 0 ]]; then
-  echo "[qemu.sh] QEMU exit code: $RET"
-  exit $RET
+  echo "[qemu.sh] QEMU exit code: $RET"
+  echo "[qemu.sh] failure-classification: $classification"
+  echo "[qemu.sh] tail(200) of serial log:"
+  tail -n 200 "$SERIAL_LOG" || true
+  exit $RET
 fi
*** End Patch

+#![allow(dead_code)]
+use core::fmt::Write;
+use crate::arch::x86_64::io::{outl, inl};
+use crate::serial;
+
+#[inline(always)]
+fn cfg_addr(bus: u8, dev: u8, func: u8, off: u8) -> u32 {
+    let aligned = (off & !3) as u32;
+    (1u32 << 31)
+        | ((bus as u32) << 16)
+        | ((dev as u32) << 11)
+        | ((func as u32) << 8)
+        | aligned
+}
+
+pub fn cfg_read32(bus: u8, dev: u8, func: u8, off: u8) -> u32 {
+    unsafe { outl(0xCF8, cfg_addr(bus, dev, func, off)); inl(0xCFC) }
+}
+
+pub fn cfg_write32(bus: u8, dev: u8, func: u8, off: u8, val: u32) {
+    unsafe { outl(0xCF8, cfg_addr(bus, dev, func, off)); outl(0xCFC, val); }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+pub struct Bdf { pub bus: u8, pub dev: u8, pub func: u8 }
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+pub struct PciId { pub vendor: u16, pub device: u16 }
+
+pub fn read_id(bdf: Bdf) -> PciId {
+    let v = cfg_read32(bdf.bus, bdf.dev, bdf.func, 0x00);
+    PciId { vendor: (v & 0xFFFF) as u16, device: ((v >> 16) & 0xFFFF) as u16 }
+}
+
+pub fn read_bar0(bdf: Bdf) -> u64 {
+    let lo = cfg_read32(bdf.bus, bdf.dev, bdf.func, 0x10);
+    let is_64 = (lo & 0b110) == 0b100;
+    let base_lo = (lo & !0xF) as u64;
+    if is_64 {
+        let hi = cfg_read32(bdf.bus, bdf.dev, bdf.func, 0x14) as u64;
+        (hi << 32) | base_lo
+    } else { base_lo }
+}
+
+pub fn find_first_e1000() -> Option<Bdf> {
+    // With QEMU `-device e1000` the default is usually 00:03.0
+    for dev in 0..32u8 {
+        let bdf = Bdf { bus: 0, dev, func: 0 };
+        let id = read_id(bdf);
+        if id.vendor == 0x8086 {
+            // Classic e1000 device IDs often 0x100e under QEMU
+            serial::write_fmt(format_args!("[pci] probe 00:{:02x}.0 vendor=0x{:04x} device=0x{:04x}\n",
+                dev, id.vendor, id.device)).ok();
+            return Some(bdf);
+        }
+    }
+    None
+}
+

+#![cfg(feature = "vfio")]
+use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
+use crate::serial;
+use crate::kernel::pci::{Bdf, read_id, read_bar0};
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+pub struct CapIommuDomain(u64);
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+pub struct CapPciDev { pub id: u64, pub bdf: Bdf }
+
+static NEXT_CAP: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
+fn new_cap() -> u64 { NEXT_CAP.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) }
+
+pub fn domain_create() -> CapIommuDomain {
+    let c = CapIommuDomain(new_cap());
+    serial::write_str("[vfio] domain created\n");
+    c
+}
+
+pub fn bind_pci(bdf: Bdf) -> Option<CapPciDev> {
+    let id = read_id(bdf);
+    if id.vendor == 0xFFFF { return None; }
+    let c = CapPciDev { id: new_cap(), bdf };
+    serial::write_fmt(format_args!(
+        "[vfio] bound {:02x}:{:02x}.{:x} vendor=0x{:04x} device=0x{:04x}\n",
+        bdf.bus, bdf.dev, bdf.func, id.vendor, id.device)).ok();
+    // BAR0 smoke (don’t actually map—just log)
+    let bar0 = read_bar0(bdf);
+    serial::write_fmt(format_args!("[vfio] bar0=0x{:016x}\n", bar0)).ok();
+    Some(c)
+}
+
+pub fn map(_dom: CapIommuDomain, iova: u64, paddr: u64, len: u64, rwx: u32) -> i32 {
+    serial::write_fmt(format_args!("[vfio] map iova=0x{:x} paddr=0x{:x} len=0x{:x} rwx=0x{:x}\n", iova, paddr, len, rwx)).ok();
+    0
+}
+pub fn unmap(_dom: CapIommuDomain, iova: u64, len: u64) -> i32 {
+    serial::write_fmt(format_args!("[vfio] unmap iova=0x{:x} len=0x{:x}\n", iova, len)).ok();
+    0
+}
+
+pub fn irq_enable(_dev: CapPciDev, _vector: u8) -> i32 {
+    // Stub: “simulate” an interrupt so the harness can validate the path.
+    serial::write_str("[vfio] irq enabled (stub)\n");
+    serial::write_str("[vfio] irq tick\n");
+    0
+}
+

+// Phase 5B (VFIO-lite)
+pub const SYS_VFIO_DOMAIN_CREATE: u64 = 0x20;
+pub const SYS_VFIO_BIND: u64 = 0x21;      // a0=bus, a1=dev, a2=func -> ret cap
+pub const SYS_VFIO_MAP: u64 = 0x22;       // a0=dom_cap, a1=iova, a2=paddr, a3=len, a4=rwx
+pub const SYS_VFIO_UNMAP: u64 = 0x23;     // a0=dom_cap, a1=iova, a2=len
+pub const SYS_VFIO_IRQ_ENABLE: u64 = 0x24;// a0=pci_cap, a1=vector
+
 pub fn syscall_dispatch(num: u64, a0: u64, a1: u64, a2: u64, a3: u64, a4: u64, _a5: u64) -> u64 {
     match num {
@@
         SYS_SPAWN_EXEC => sys_spawn_exec(a0 as *const u8, a1 as usize) as u64,
+        #[cfg(feature = "vfio")]
+        SYS_VFIO_DOMAIN_CREATE => {
+            let c = crate::kernel::vfio::domain_create();
+            c.0
+        }
+        #[cfg(feature = "vfio")]
+        SYS_VFIO_BIND => {
+            let bdf = crate::kernel::pci::Bdf{ bus: a0 as u8, dev: a1 as u8, func: a2 as u8 };
+            match crate::kernel::vfio::bind_pci(bdf) {
+                Some(c) => c.id,
+                None => u64::MAX
+            }
+        }
+        #[cfg(feature = "vfio")]
+        SYS_VFIO_MAP => crate::kernel::vfio::map(
+            crate::kernel::vfio::CapIommuDomain(a0), a1, a2, a3, a4 as u32) as u64,
+        #[cfg(feature = "vfio")]
+        SYS_VFIO_UNMAP => crate::kernel::vfio::unmap(
+            crate::kernel::vfio::CapIommuDomain(a0), a1, a2) as u64,
+        #[cfg(feature = "vfio")]
+        SYS_VFIO_IRQ_ENABLE => crate::kernel::vfio::irq_enable(
+            crate::kernel::vfio::CapPciDev{ id: a0, bdf: crate::kernel::pci::Bdf{ bus:0,dev:0,func:0}}, a1 as u8) as u64,
         _ => u64::MAX,
     }
 }

+    if rc != 0 { fail(0x63); }
+    serial::write_str("[vfio-test] bind_list ok\n");
+}
+
+pub fn run_irq_smoke() {
+    serial::write_str("[vfio-test] irq_smoke start\n");
+    let _dom = sys(SYS_VFIO_DOMAIN_CREATE,0,0,0,0,0);
+    let cap = sys(SYS_VFIO_BIND, 0,3,0,0,0);
+    if cap == u64::MAX { fail(0x64); }
+    let rc = sys(SYS_VFIO_IRQ_ENABLE, cap, 1,0,0,0);
+    if rc != 0 { fail(0x65); }
+    serial::write_str("[vfio-test] irq_smoke ok\n");
+}
+

+    crate::kernel::qemu_exit::fail(code);
+    loop { crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::halt(); }

Short answer: yes—but it’s a port, not a flip of a switch. It’s doable after the x86_64 kernel is “feature-complete,” and the path runs through the Asahi Linux toolchain and docs.

Here’s the real picture in plain English:

What changes (architecture)
CPU/ISA: x86_64 → ARM64 (AArch64). All low-level bits change: exceptions, syscalls, page tables, TLB, caches, barriers, atomic rules.

Boot & firmware: No PC BIOS/UEFI. Apple uses iBoot. Practical route: boot as a payload via m1n1 (Asahi’s loader) and/or their UEFI shim. That gives you something UEFI-ish to stand on.

Interrupts/timers: APIC/IOAPIC/LAPIC → Apple AIC (custom interrupt controller) + ARM generic timer (CNTV_*). Different registers, different init.

Paging/MMU: x86_64 4-level pages → ARM64 translation tables (4K/16K/64K pages), different access flags, PAN/UXN/PXN instead of NX, etc.

Exceptions/syscalls: int 0x80/IDT → vector table + SVC (Supervisor Call). Fault decoding is different but maps cleanly to our PFM ideas.

SMP bring-up: INIT/SIPI → spin tables/ PSCI-like bring-up via m1n1; you start at EL1 (not EL2), with some privileges constrained.

IOMMU/PCIe: VT-d → DART (Apple’s IOMMU). PCIe controller is Apple-specific. Your VFIO/IOMMU layer becomes a new backend.

GPU: Apple GPU is proprietary. Treat it as non-VFIO for now; focus on NIC/USB/PCIe dev boards first.

What stays conceptually the same
The microkernel shape: per-task address spaces, capability IPC, preemptive scheduler, userland services.

Your PFM discipline and test harness approach: same strategy, different exception codes.

The userland model: ELF64, VFS/initfs, spawn/exit/wait—mostly portable.

Feasible plan (after x86_64 is done)
Create an arch/aarch64 tree next to x86_64. Keep all higher-level code untouched.

Boot via m1n1 (chainload) or Asahi’s UEFI shim. Start with serial/USB-C prints → proof of life → panic path.

Minimal bring-up: MMU on (identity map + kernel higher half), vector table, timer tick (CNTV), simple IRQ via AIC, SVC handler.

Port your primitives: page-fault handler → ARM sync aborts; syscall gate → SVC; scheduler tick → generic timer; SMP → m1n1 CPU start helper.

PFM v1/v2 on ARM: re-express the matrix with ARM page bits (UXN/PXN, AP[RW], user/supervisor). Make all tests green.

Userland boot: ELF loader tweaks (AArch64 ABI), ring-3 trampoline via eret frames, capability IPC unchanged.

IOMMU/VFIO (later): new backend for DART; start with safe “deny all DMA,” then map a simple PCIe device supported by Asahi stack.

Realistic constraints
You’ll almost certainly run at EL1 under m1n1 (hypervisor EL2 is not freely available), which is fine for an OS.

Apple GPU passthrough is a long-term project; plan your dual-GPU “Philosophy/Technical” concept on discrete PCIe GPUs attached to compatible Macs or external enclosures first.

Some Apple SoC blocks are undocumented; lean on Asahi docs and reuse their device trees.

Effort level (after x86_64 is done)
Small team, focused: 6–10 weeks to first userland “hello” on Apple Silicon (serial, timer, IRQs, PFM green).

VFIO/DART: add 4–8+ weeks, depending on how deep you go and what hardware you’re targeting.

The bottleneck isn’t your kernel design—it’s Apple-specific hardware bring-up.

Bottom line
Yes, you can make a specialized Apple Silicon build of SIS once the x86_64 kernel is complete. Do it by adding an AArch64/Apple port layer, booting through m1n1/Asahi UEFI, and re-implementing the low-level backends (boot, exceptions, MMU, interrupts, timer, IOMMU). Your microkernel architecture, capability IPC, scheduler, VFS, and test-driven methodology transfer very well.

+    pub fn e1000_trigger_msi(bar0: *mut u8) {

+pub fn cfg_read16(bdf: Bdf, off: u16) -> Result<u16, i32> {
+    let w = cfg_read32(bdf, (off & !2) as u16)?; // aligned dword
+    let shift = (off & 2) * 8;
+    Ok(((w >> shift) & 0xFFFF) as u16)
+}
+#[inline]
+pub fn cfg_write16(bdf: Bdf, off: u16, val: u16) -> Result<(), i32> {
+    let dwoff = (off & !2) as u16;
+    let old = cfg_read32(bdf, dwoff)?;
+    let shift = (off & 2) * 8;
+    let mask = !(0xFFFFu32 << shift);
+    let new = (old & mask) | ((val as u32) << shift);
+    cfg_write32(bdf, dwoff, new)
+}

 //! VFIO end-to-end MSI delivery: arm -> trigger -> see IRQ -> disarm -> verify silence.
 
 use crate::serial;
 use crate::kernel::syscall;
 use crate::kernel::pci::{Bdf};
+use crate::kernel::vfio::vfio::{e1000_trigger_msi, vfio_irq_count, VFIO_VECTOR};
+use crate::arch::x86_64::cpu;
 
 pub fn run_vfio_msi_smoke() -> i32 {
     serial::write_str("[selftest] VFIO_MSI_SMOKE start\n");
 
     // 1) Bind device (assumes helper exists; else enumerate & pick 00:03.0)
     let bdf = Bdf { bus: 0, dev: 3, func: 0 };
     let h = syscall::vfio_bind(bdf);
     if h < 0 { serial::write_str("[selftest] bind failed\n"); return 0x71; }
 
     // 2) Create domain + staging + enable bus master (existing syscalls)
     if syscall::vfio_domain_create(h) != 0 { serial::write_str("[selftest] domain fail\n"); return 0x72; }
     if syscall::vfio_domain_map_staging(h, 16 * 1024) != 0 { serial::write_str("[selftest] staging fail\n"); return 0x73; }
     if syscall::vfio_enable_busmaster(h) != 0 { serial::write_str("[selftest] busmaster fail\n"); return 0x74; }
 
     // 3) Map BAR0 (RW); get host pointer for MMIO pokes
     let bar0 = syscall::vfio_map_bar(h, 0);
     if bar0.is_null() { serial::write_str("[selftest] map BAR0 failed\n"); return 0x75; }
 
     // 4) Arm MSI (vector 0x5E)
     if syscall::vfio_msi_arm(h, VFIO_VECTOR) != 0 { serial::write_str("[selftest] msi arm fail\n"); return 0x76; }
 
     // 5) Trigger MSI via e1000 ICS poke
     let before = vfio_irq_count();
     e1000_trigger_msi(bar0);
 
     // 6) Wait up to ~10ms for first IRQ
     let t0 = cpu::rdtsc();
     let mut seen = false;
     for _ in 0..5000 {
         let c = vfio_irq_count();
         if c > before {
             seen = true; break;
         }
         cpu::pause();
     }
     if !seen { serial::write_str("[selftest] no IRQ delivered\n"); return 0x77; }
     serial::write_str("[selftest] irq delivered\n");
 
     // 7) Disarm and verify silence (~2ms window)
     if syscall::vfio_msi_disarm(h) != 0 { serial::write_str("[selftest] msi disarm fail\n"); return 0x78; }
     let post = vfio_irq_count();
     let t1 = cpu::rdtsc();
     let mut silent = true;
     for _ in 0..1000 {
         if vfio_irq_count() != post { silent = false; break; }
         cpu::pause();
     }
     if !silent { serial::write_str("[selftest] IRQ after disarm\n"); return 0x79; }
 
     serial::write_str("[selftest] VFIO_MSI_SMOKE ok\n");
     0x00
 }

Notes & rationale (quick):
e1000 MSI trigger: QEMU’s e1000 accepts a software interrupt via ICS when the matching bit is masked-in via IMS. Setting bit0 in both is a reliable software-only cause; we clear stale ICR first for cleanliness.

INTx disable: Set PCI Command bit10 on arm; clear it on disarm, so MSI is exclusive.

Rate-limited logs: count & 63 == 1 prints every 64th hit; keeps CI logs sane but preserves visibility.

Spurious guard: VFIO_IRQ_ARMED epoch goes nonzero on arm and zero on disarm. ISR ignores late arrivals after disarm, but still EOIs.

Selftest: Pure MMIO trigger—no real traffic required. It asserts “no further IRQs” within a short window after disarm.

If you want this split into three commits (Trigger, ISR, Selftest) for clean history, say the word and I’ll format into three separate patches with commit messages.

+//! Tiny per-CPU IRQ vector allocator for MSI-style dynamic vectors.
+//! Reserves 0x50..=0x5F inclusive per CPU. Bitmap-based, lock-free.
+
+use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU16, Ordering};
+use spin::Once;
+
+const BASE: u8 = 0x50;
+const COUNT: usize = 16; // 0x50..=0x5F
+
+static INIT: Once<()> = Once::new();
+static PERCPU_BITMAPS: Once<&'static [AtomicU16]> = Once::new();
+
+fn init() {
+    INIT.call_once(|| {
+        // For now assume a small CPU count already discovered by LAPIC init
+        let ncpu = crate::kernel::cpu::cpu_count();
+        let slice = {
+            let ptr = crate::kernel::alloc::kalloc_array::<AtomicU16>(ncpu);
+            // zeroed = all free
+            unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, ncpu) }
+        };
+        PERCPU_BITMAPS.call_once(|| slice);
+    });
+}
+
+fn bm(cpu: usize) -> &'static AtomicU16 {
+    init();
+    &PERCPU_BITMAPS.get().unwrap()[cpu]
+}
+
+#[inline]
+fn bit_for(vec: u8) -> u16 { 1u16 << (vec - BASE) }
+
+#[inline]
+pub fn range() -> core::ops::RangeInclusive<u8> { BASE..=BASE + (COUNT as u8 - 1) }
+
+/// Allocate a free vector on this CPU. Returns vector or None.
+pub fn alloc_vector(cpu: usize) -> Option<u8> {
+    let m = bm(cpu);
+    loop {
+        let cur = m.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+        if cur == 0xFFFF { return None; } // full
+        // find first zero bit
+        let mut free_idx = None;
+        for i in 0..COUNT {
+            if (cur & (1u16 << i)) == 0 { free_idx = Some(i); break; }
+        }
+        let idx = free_idx?;
+        let new = cur | (1u16 << idx);
+        if m.compare_exchange(cur, new, Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Relaxed).is_ok() {
+            return Some(BASE + idx as u8);
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Free a previously allocated vector on this CPU.
+pub fn free_vector(cpu: usize, vec: u8) {
+    if !(range().contains(&vec)) { return; }
+    let m = bm(cpu);
+    loop {
+        let cur = m.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let new = cur & !bit_for(vec);
+        if m.compare_exchange(cur, new, Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Relaxed).is_ok() { return; }
+    }
+}
+

+/// Install / replace a handler at an arbitrary vector at runtime.
+pub fn install_runtime_isr(vector: u8, f: extern "x86-interrupt" fn(InterruptStackFrame)) {
+    use x86_64::structures::idt::Entry;
+    let idt = IDT.get().expect("IDT not init");
+    // SAFETY: we only touch the chosen slot
+    let entry: &mut Entry<extern "x86-interrupt" fn(InterruptStackFrame)> =
+        unsafe { &mut *(&idt[vector as usize] as *const _ as *mut _) };
+    entry.set_handler_fn(f);
+}
+
+#[inline(always)]
+fn tsc() -> u64 { unsafe { core::arch::x86_64::_rdtsc() } }
+
+/// Unified VFIO ISR that looks up the handle by vector, rate-limits logs, updates latency histogram.
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+extern "x86-interrupt" fn vfio_irq_common(_sf: InterruptStackFrame) {
+    use crate::arch::x86_64::lapic;
+    use crate::kernel::vfio;
+    let vec = lapic::last_vector(); // or pass via per-cpu if you cache it; fallback to a stored slot
+    let now = tsc();
+    if let Some((h, epoch)) = vfio::lookup_by_vector(vec) {
+        let (count, t_trigger) = vfio::on_irq(h, epoch, now);
+        if (count & 63) == 0 {
+            serial::write_str("[vfio-irq] vec=");
+            serial::write_hex_u8(vec);
+            serial::write_str(" count=");
+            serial::write_hex_u64(count);
+            serial::write_str("\n");
+        }
+        if t_trigger != 0 && now >= t_trigger {
+            vfio_rt::hist_add(now - t_trigger);
+        }
+    } else {
+        // spurious / late
+        serial::write_str("[vfio-irq] spurious vec=");
+        serial::write_hex_u8(vec);
+        serial::write_str("\n");
+    }
+    lapic::eoi();
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_isr_vector_install(vec: u8) { install_runtime_isr(vec, vfio_irq_common); }
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_unmap_vector(vec: u8) { vfio_rt::unmap_vector(vec); }
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_map_vector(vec: u8, packed: u64) { vfio_rt::map_vector(vec, packed); }
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_dump_hist() { vfio_rt::dump_hist(); }

+    if cnt2 != cnt { ok = false; serial_print!("[vfio-soak] disarm not silent\n"); }

+//! Per-CPU MSI vector allocator for 0x50..=0x5F.
+//! Simple bitmap per CPU; lock-free with Atomics.
+
+use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU16, Ordering};
+use spin::Once;
+
+const BASE: u8 = 0x50;
+const COUNT: usize = 16; // 0x50..=0x5F
+const MAX_CPUS: usize = 8; // conservative cap; adjust if your cpu_count() > 8
+
+static INIT: Once<()> = Once::new();
+static mut BITMAPS: [AtomicU16; MAX_CPUS] = [
+    AtomicU16::new(0); MAX_CPUS
+];
+
+fn ensure_init() {
+    INIT.call_once(|| {
+        // Nothing dynamic to do; placeholder for parity with other init flows.
+    });
+}
+
+#[inline] pub fn range() -> core::ops::RangeInclusive<u8> { BASE..=BASE + (COUNT as u8 - 1) }
+
+#[inline]
+fn bit_for(vec: u8) -> u16 { 1u16 << (vec - BASE) }
+
+#[inline]
+fn idx_for_cpu(cpu: usize) -> usize {
+    // Clamp to MAX_CPUS-1 if cpu_count() exceeds cap.
+    if cpu < MAX_CPUS { cpu } else { MAX_CPUS - 1 }
+}
+
+/// Allocate a free vector on this CPU. Returns vector or None.
+pub fn alloc_vector(cpu: usize) -> Option<u8> {
+    ensure_init();
+    let i = idx_for_cpu(cpu);
+    let m = unsafe { &BITMAPS[i] };
+    loop {
+        let cur = m.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+        if cur == 0xFFFF { return None; } // full
+        // find first zero bit within COUNT
+        let mut free = None;
+        for b in 0..COUNT {
+            if (cur & (1u16 << b)) == 0 { free = Some(b); break; }
+        }
+        let b = free?;
+        let new = cur | (1u16 << b);
+        if m.compare_exchange(cur, new, Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Relaxed).is_ok() {
+            return Some(BASE + b as u8);
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Free a previously allocated vector on this CPU.
+pub fn free_vector(cpu: usize, vec: u8) {
+    ensure_init();
+    if !range().contains(&vec) { return; }
+    let i = idx_for_cpu(cpu);
+    let m = unsafe { &BITMAPS[i] };
+    loop {
+        let cur = m.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let new = cur & !bit_for(vec);
+        if m.compare_exchange(cur, new, Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Relaxed).is_ok() { return; }
+    }
+}
+

+    static HIST: [AtomicU64; 16] = unsafe { core::mem::zeroed() };
+
+    #[inline] pub fn map(vec: u8, packed: u64) { VEC_PACKED[vec as usize].store(packed, Ordering::Release); }
+    #[inline] pub fn unmap(vec: u8) { VEC_PACKED[vec as usize].store(0, Ordering::Release); }
+    #[inline] pub fn load(vec: u8) -> u64 { VEC_PACKED[vec as usize].load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) }
+
+    #[inline]
+    fn bucket(cycles: u64) -> usize {
+        if cycles == 0 { return 0; }
+        let l = 63 - cycles.leading_zeros() as usize;
+        core::cmp::min(l, 15)
+    }
+    #[inline]
+    pub fn hist_add(cycles: u64) {
+        HIST[bucket(cycles)].fetch_add(1, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
+    }
+    pub fn dump_hist() {
+        serial::write_str("[vfio-lat] buckets(log2 cycles): ");
+        for i in 0..16 {
+            let v = HIST[i].load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
+            crate::serial::write_hex_u8(i as u8);
+            serial::write_str("=");
+            crate::serial::write_hex_u64(v);
+            serial::write_str(" ");
+        }
+        serial::write_str("\n");
+    }
+    pub fn packed_load(vec: u8) -> u64 { load(vec) }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_map_vector(vec: u8, packed: u64) { vfio_rt::map(vec, packed) }
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_unmap_vector(vec: u8) { vfio_rt::unmap(vec) }
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_vector_packed_load(vec: u8) -> u64 { vfio_rt::packed_load(vec) }
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+pub fn vfio_dump_hist() { vfio_rt::dump_hist() }

+// ----- VFIO ISR macro: generate 16 handlers (0x50..=0x5F) that pass vector id -----
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+macro_rules! make_vfio_isr {
+    ($name:ident, $vec:expr) => {
+        extern "x86-interrupt" fn $name(_sf: InterruptStackFrame) {
+            // Fast path: look up handle+epoch from vector mapping
+            let vec = $vec as u8;
+            let packed = super::idt::vfio_vector_packed_load(vec);
+            if packed != 0 {
+                let handle = crate::kernel::vfio::VfioHandle((packed & 0xFFFF) as u16);
+                let epoch = (packed >> 16) & 0xFFFF_FFFF;
+                let now = rdtsc();
+                let (count, t_trig) = crate::kernel::vfio::on_irq(handle, epoch, now);
+                if (count & 63) == 0 {
+                    crate::serial::write_str("[vfio-irq] vec=");
+                    crate::serial::write_hex_u8(vec);
+                    crate::serial::write_str(" count=");
+                    crate::serial::write_hex_u64(count);
+                    crate::serial::write_str("\n");
+                }
+                if t_trig != 0 && now >= t_trig {
+                    super::idt::vfio_rt::hist_add(now - t_trig);
+                }
+            } else {
+                crate::serial::write_str("[vfio-irq] spurious vec=");
+                crate::serial::write_hex_u8($vec as u8);
+                crate::serial::write_str("\n");
+            }
+            crate::arch::x86_64::lapic::eoi();
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature="vfio")]
+mod vfio_isrs {
+    use super::*;
+    make_vfio_isr!(vfio_vec_50, 0x50);
+    make_vfio_isr!(vfio_vec_51, 0x51);
+    make_vfio_isr!(vfio_vec_52, 0x52);
+    make_vfio_isr!(vfio_vec_53, 0x53);
+    make_vfio_isr!(vfio_vec_54, 0x54);

+            0x5E => Some(vfio_vec_5E),
+            0x5F => Some(vfio_vec_5F),
+            _ => None,

+    }

+/// Soak test: 100 MSI triggers spaced ~10ms. Verifies count parity and silence after disarm.
+fn selftest_vfio_msi_soak() {
+    use crate::sys::*;
+    serial_print!("[vfio-soak] begin\n");
+    let h = sys_vfio_bind_first_e1000().expect("bind");
+    sys_vfio_domain_create(h).expect("dom");
+    sys_vfio_dma_stage(h, 16*1024).expect("stage");
+    sys_vfio_enable_busmaster(h).expect("bm");
+    sys_vfio_msi_arm(h).expect("arm");
+    let iters = 100u64;
+    for _ in 0..iters {
+        sys_vfio_msi_trigger_e1000(h).expect("trig");
+        sys_sleep_ms(10);
+    }
+    let cnt = sys_vfio_irq_count(h).unwrap_or(0);
+    serial_print!("[vfio-soak] count={} iters={}\n", cnt, iters);
+    let mut ok = true;
+    if cnt < iters {
+        ok = false;
+        serial_print!("[vfio-soak] undercount\n");
+    }
+    sys_vfio_msi_disarm(h).ok();
+    // post-disarm silence verification
+    sys_vfio_msi_trigger_e1000(h).ok();
+    sys_sleep_ms(10);
+    let cnt2 = sys_vfio_irq_count(h).unwrap_or(0);
+    if cnt2 != cnt {
+        ok = false;
+        serial_print!("[vfio-soak] disarm not silent\n");
+    }
+    // dump latency histogram
+    unsafe { crate::arch::x86_64::idt::vfio_dump_hist(); }
+    if ok { qemu_exit_success(); } else { qemu_exit_code(0x6F); }
+}

You’re running into QEMU’s “-kernel expects a Linux bzImage or a PVH ELF” trap. Our kernel ELF is a freestanding Rust binary, not a Linux image and not PVH-annotated, so QEMU refuses to load it directly. That’s why you see:

qemu-system-x86_64: Error loading uncompressed kernel without PVH ELF Note
The fix (quick + reliable)
Stop using -kernel. Boot the disk image produced by bootimage (BIOS path). You already locked to bootloader = 0.10.x, which is perfect for this.

One-time setup (if not done yet)
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none
rustup component add rust-src
cargo install bootimage --version 0.10.3
Build the bootable image
# Include whatever features you need (e.g. vfio, userland, …)
cargo +nightly-2024-12-15 bootimage --features "vfio userland"
This creates:

target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/bootimage-<crate-name>.bin
Run with QEMU (BIOS/text mode)
qemu-system-x86_64 \
  -machine q35,accel=kvm:tcg \
  -cpu qemu64 \
  -m 1024 \
  -no-reboot -no-shutdown \
  -serial file:out/qemu-serial.log \
  -device isa-debug-exit,iobase=0xf4,iosize=0x04 \
  -drive format=raw,file=target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/bootimage-<crate-name>.bin \
  -display none
That will bypass PVH entirely and you should see your usual banners in out/qemu-serial.log (and your VFIO soak test logs) as soon as the kernel enters kernel_main().

Drop-in script tweak (so you don’t have to remember this)
If your scripts/qemu.sh is still using -kernel, switch it to the bootimage artifact. Minimal diff:

- KERNEL_ELF="target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/<crate-name>"
+ BOOTBIN="target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/bootimage-<crate-name>.bin"

- qemu-system-x86_64 ... -kernel "$KERNEL_ELF" ...
+ qemu-system-x86_64 ... -drive format=raw,file="$BOOTBIN" ...
And ensure the script builds it first:

cargo +nightly-2024-12-15 bootimage --features "$FEATURES" $CARGO_EXTRA_ARGS
(If you want, I can send a tiny qemu.sh patch that: builds via bootimage, locates the produced .bin, and auto-switches in -device e1000 / -device intel-iommu,intremap=on when TEST=VFIO_* is set.)

Alternative paths (only if you really need them)
UEFI path (bootloader 0.11.x + OVMF): works too, but you previously hit the VESA path hang. You can revisit later with a minimal UEFI config and OVMF, but BIOS + 0.10.x is the fastest path to green.

PVH direct boot (-kernel): possible, but you’d need to add a Xen PVH note (or use a PVH shim). That’s extra plumbing and offers no benefit right now.

Why this fixes your exact error
-kernel tells QEMU: “this is a Linux/pvh bootable image.” Our ELF isn’t either, so QEMU aborts before any code runs → empty serial log → your “pre-entry” failure classification. Booting the raw disk image produced by bootimage puts SeaBIOS in front, which happily loads the bootloader, which then jumps to our kernel_main() in plain text mode—no PVH/graphics required.

Once you switch to the bootimage .bin, your VFIO_MSI_SOAK test should finally run and produce the histogram/soak logs we wired up.

Option B (robust): Generate the disk image yourself in build.rs
This bypasses bootimage entirely and calls the bootloader’s builder API directly (v0.10.12). It’s stable and keeps everything under your control.

Cargo.toml

build.rs (minimal, BIOS text-mode)

use std::{env, path::PathBuf};

fn main() {
    // Path to the kernel ELF built by Cargo
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR").unwrap());
    let kernel = out_dir.join("../../../..").join("x86_64-unknown-none").join("debug").join("<your-crate-name>");

    // Where to place the disk image
    let image_path = PathBuf::from("target/boot-bios.img");

    // Build a BIOS/text-mode image; for 0.10.x this uses the builder inside the bootloader crate
    bootloader::BiosBoot::new()
        .kernel(&kernel)
        .create_disk_image(&image_path)
        .expect("failed to create BIOS disk image");

    // Rebuild if the kernel binary changes
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", kernel.display());
}

  -device isa-debug-exit,iobase=0xf4,iosize=0x04 \
  -drive format=raw,file=target/boot-bios.img \
  -display none

The PVH/PVH-note error only happens when you pass -kernel a non-Linux ELF. Using a disk image (from bootimage or your own build.rs) boots via BIOS → bootloader → your kernel_main(). No PVH involved, no VESA path, text mode only.

The package.metadata.bootloader.target complaint comes from bootimage expecting a bootloader with that internal key. Pinning bootloader = 0.10.12 with bootimage = 0.10.3 avoids that mismatch.

use std::{env, fs, path::PathBuf};

fn main() {
    // Ensure we rebuild image whenever the kernel binary changes
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");

    // Where cargo puts the compiled kernel ELF
    let target_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("CARGO_TARGET_DIR").unwrap_or_else(|_| "target".into()));
    let profile = env::var("PROFILE").unwrap(); // debug/release
    let target = "x86_64-unknown-none";

    // Kernel ELF path (produced by cargo build)
    // NOTE: replace `sis-kernel` with your actual crate name if different
    let kernel_elf = target_dir
        .join(target)
        .join(&profile)
        .join("sis-kernel");

    // Output bootable image path
    let out_img = target_dir.join("boot-bios.img");

    // Build config: disable framebuffer to force plain BIOS text mode
    let mut config = bootloader::BootConfig::default();
    // Turn off framebuffer/graphics completely
    config.framebuffer = None;

    // Optional: speed up debug builds (don’t relocate kernel for ASLR)
    // config.relocate_kernel = false;

    // Make sure the kernel ELF exists before we call the builder
    if !kernel_elf.exists() {
        // In the first build run, the ELF may not be present yet; just return.
        // The second cargo invocation (or `cargo build` re-run) will create the image.
        return;
    }

    // Create BIOS disk image (no UEFI path at all)
    bootloader::BiosBoot::new(config)
        .create_disk_image(&kernel_elf, &out_img)
        .expect("failed to create BIOS disk image");

    // Ensure the `target/boot-bios.img` exists for qemu.sh
    println!("cargo:warning=Bootable BIOS image written to {}", out_img.display());
}

We explicitly disable framebuffer (config.framebuffer = None), so you don’t hit the VESA path that previously froze.

If you want strict one-shot behavior, you can make build.rs shell-out to cargo build first, but keeping build.rs pure is cleaner.

In your memory init (where you currently do OffsetPageTable with .unwrap()), switch to:

use x86_64::structures::paging::{Mapper, OffsetPageTable, MappedPageTable};
use x86_64::{VirtAddr, registers::control::Cr3};
use bootloader_api::BootInfo;

pub enum AnyMapper<'a> {
    Offset(OffsetPageTable<'a>),
    Recursive(MappedPageTable<'a>),
}

pub unsafe fn init_mapper(boot_info: &bootloader_api::BootInfo) -> AnyMapper<'static> {
    // SAFETY: we are in early boot, single core
    let (level4_frame, _) = Cr3::read();

    if let Some(off) = boot_info.physical_memory_offset.into_option() {
        // Legacy style: phys-mem window
        let l4_table_ptr = (off + level4_frame.start_address().as_u64()).as_mut_ptr();
        let l4_table = &mut *l4_table_ptr;
        AnyMapper::Offset(OffsetPageTable::new(l4_table, VirtAddr::new(off.as_u64())))
    } else if let Some(rec_idx) = boot_info.recursive_index.into_option() {
        // 0.11 style: recursive mapping
        let l4_table_virt = VirtAddr::new(((rec_idx as u64) << 39) | ((rec_idx as u64) << 30) | ((rec_idx as u64) << 21) | ((rec_idx as u64) << 12));
        let l4_table = &mut *l4_table_virt.as_mut_ptr();
        AnyMapper::Recursive(MappedPageTable::new(l4_table))
    } else {
        // Neither provided: bail loudly with a clear message
        crate::serial::write_str("[mm] no phys_offset and no recursive_index; cannot init mapper\n");
        loop { crate::cpu::halt(); }
    }
}

Here’s a focused, step-by-step fix plan that has rescued a lot of 0.11 boots.

1) Make BootInfo handling 0.11-correct (stop unwrapping offset)
In 0.11 there’s no config knob to “turn on” a physical memory offset window. Treat it as optional and prefer recursive mapping if provided.

use bootloader_api::BootInfo;
use x86_64::{VirtAddr, registers::control::Cr3};
use x86_64::structures::paging::{OffsetPageTable, MappedPageTable, Mapper};

enum MapperAny<'a> { Offset(OffsetPageTable<'a>), Rec(MappedPageTable<'a>) }

unsafe fn init_mapper(boot: &BootInfo) -> MapperAny<'static> {
    let (l4_frame, _) = Cr3::read();

    if let Some(off) = boot.physical_memory_offset.into_option() {
        let l4_ptr = (off + l4_frame.start_address().as_u64()).as_mut_ptr();
        let l4 = &mut *l4_ptr;
        MapperAny::Offset(OffsetPageTable::new(l4, VirtAddr::new(off.as_u64())))
    } else if let Some(idx) = boot.recursive_index.into_option() {
        // common 0.11 path
        let va = VirtAddr::new(((idx as u64) << 39)
                             | ((idx as u64) << 30)
                             | ((idx as u64) << 21)
                             | ((idx as u64) << 12));
        let l4 = &mut *va.as_mut_ptr();
        MapperAny::Rec(MappedPageTable::new(l4))
    } else {
        crate::serial::write_str("[mm] no phys_offset and no recursive_index\n");
        loop { crate::cpu::halt(); }
    }
}

use x86_64::structures::idt::{InterruptDescriptorTable, InterruptStackFrame};

// divide by zero
extern "x86-interrupt" fn isr_div0(_sf: InterruptStackFrame) { /* ... */ }

// page fault
extern "x86-interrupt" fn isr_pf(sf: InterruptStackFrame,
    _ec: x86_64::structures::idt::PageFaultErrorCode) { /* ... */ }

// double fault (your transmute workaround stays)
extern "x86-interrupt" fn isr_df(_sf: InterruptStackFrame, _ec: u64) {
    loop { crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::halt(); }
}

static mut IDT: Option<InterruptDescriptorTable> = None;

fn init_idt() {
    let mut idt = InterruptDescriptorTable::new();
    idt.divide_error.set_handler_fn(isr_div0);
    idt.page_fault.set_handler_fn(isr_pf);

    // DF wants -> ! in x86_64 0.14.x, but the compiler forbids returns.
    // keep your cast at *registration* time:
    let df_ptr_no_ret: extern "x86-interrupt" fn(InterruptStackFrame, u64) =
        isr_df; // () returning fn item
    let df_ptr_never: extern "x86-interrupt" fn(InterruptStackFrame, u64) -> ! =
        unsafe { core::mem::transmute(df_ptr_no_ret) };
    idt.double_fault.set_handler_fn(df_ptr_never);

    // VFIO MSI vector, e.g. 0x5E
    idt[0x5e].set_handler_fn(crate::kernel::vfio::vfio_irq_handler);

    unsafe { IDT = Some(idt); IDT.as_ref().unwrap().load(); }
}

Awesome—here are the two drop-in snippets you asked for. They do exactly one thing: guarantee boot_info.physical_memory_offset is populated (via Mapping::Dynamic) and wire your kernel’s mapper to use it, with a clean fallback to recursive mapping if you ever enable that later.

build.rs (bootloader 0.11.x, BIOS image, Dynamic phys map)
// build.rs
// Generates a BIOS-bootable disk image using bootloader 0.11.x
// and requests Dynamic physical memory mapping so the kernel
// sees boot_info.physical_memory_offset = Some(offset).

use std::{env, fs, path::PathBuf};
use bootloader::{BiosBoot, BootConfig};
use bootloader::config::{Mapping, LogLevel};

fn main() {
    // Always rebuild the image when the kernel changes
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src/");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=Cargo.toml");

    // Path to the kernel ELF we’re building (debug or release)
    // Adjust profile detection if you want; this keeps it simple.
    let profile = env::var("PROFILE").unwrap_or_else(|_| "debug".into());
    let mut kernel_elf = PathBuf::from("target");
    kernel_elf.push("x86_64-unknown-none");
    kernel_elf.push(&profile);
    kernel_elf.push("sis_kernel"); // your kernel crate name/binary

    // Output image path (scripts/qemu.sh expects this).
    let mut out_dir = PathBuf::from("out");
    fs::create_dir_all(&out_dir).ok();
    let img_path = out_dir.join("sis-bios.img");

    // Boot config:
    // - Dynamic physical mapping (populates BootInfo.physical_memory_offset)
    // - Serial logging enabled (early bootloader messages to serial)
    // - Framebuffer logging disabled (avoid VESA path)
    let mut cfg = BootConfig::default();
    cfg.log_level = LogLevel::Info;
    cfg.serial_logging = true;
    cfg.frame_buffer_logging = false;
    // This is the key line that fixes your mapper:
    cfg.mappings.physical_memory = Some(Mapping::Dynamic);

    // Build BIOS image
    let mut bios = BiosBoot::new(&kernel_elf);
    bios.set_boot_config(&cfg);
    bios.set_disk_image_path(&img_path); // ensure known filename
    bios.build().expect("bootloader build failed");

    println!("cargo:warning=Boot image written to {}", img_path.display());
}
If your bootloader 0.11.x doesn’t have .set_disk_image_path(), drop that line—build() will still write a default image (usually in target/…). Update your qemu.sh to point at whatever it prints. The rest stays the same.

memory.rs (use phys_offset if present; clean fallback; loud logs)
// src/arch/x86_64/memory.rs
#![allow(dead_code)]

use x86_64::{
    VirtAddr, PhysAddr,
    registers::control::Cr3,
    structures::paging::{
        OffsetPageTable, PageTable, PhysFrame, FrameAllocator, Size4KiB,
    },
};
use bootloader_api::BootInfo;

use crate::kernel::serial;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

/// Global boot-time mapper once initialized.
static mut BOOT_MAPPER: Option<OffsetPageTable<'static>> = None;

/// SAFETY: caller must ensure `phys_offset` corresponds to a valid linear mapping of physical memory.
unsafe fn init_offset_page_table(phys_offset: VirtAddr) -> OffsetPageTable<'static> {
    let (frame, _) = Cr3::read();
    let phys = frame.start_address();
    let virt = phys_offset + phys.as_u64();
    let l4: *mut PageTable = virt.as_mut_ptr();
    OffsetPageTable::new(&mut *l4, phys_offset)
}

/// Initialize paging mapper from BootInfo:
/// 1) Prefer physical_memory_offset (bootloader 0.11.x + Mapping::Dynamic)
/// 2) (Optional) If you later enable recursive mapping, handle recursive_index here
/// Panics loudly if neither is provided.
pub fn init_boot_mappings(boot_info: &'static BootInfo) {
    serial::write_str("[mem] boot mapping options: pmo=");
    match boot_info.physical_memory_offset.into_option() {
        Some(off) => {
            serial::write_str("some, ri=none\n");
            let off = VirtAddr::new(off);
            unsafe {
                let mapper = init_offset_page_table(off);
                BOOT_MAPPER = Some(mapper);
            }
            serial::write_str("[mem] OffsetPageTable initialized (PhysicalMemory=Dynamic)\n");
            return;
        }
        None => {
            // Keep the log shape stable:
            serial::write_str("none, ri=");
            match boot_info.recursive_index.into_option() {
                Some(ri) => {
                    serial::write_hex8(ri as u8);
                    serial::write_str("\n");
                    // If/when you enable recursive mapping mode, initialize it here.
                    // For now, we fail loudly because we rely on Mapping::Dynamic.
                    serial::write_str("[mem] recursive mapping path not implemented in this build\n");
                }
                None => {
                    serial::write_str("none\n");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // If we got here, neither mapping was usable. Halt with a loud message.
    serial::write_str("[mem][FATAL] No physical memory mapping available (enable Mapping::Dynamic in build.rs)\n");
    loop { crate::kernel::cpu::halt(); }
}

/// Borrow the mapper (panic if not initialized).
pub fn mapper() -> &'static mut OffsetPageTable<'static> {
    unsafe { BOOT_MAPPER.as_mut().expect("BOOT_MAPPER not initialized") }
}

/// Minimal frame allocator stub wired to BootInfo; replace with your real allocator.
pub struct BootInfoFrameAllocator;

unsafe impl FrameAllocator<Size4KiB> for BootInfoFrameAllocator {
    fn allocate_frame(&mut self) -> Option<PhysFrame> {
        // Plug in your frame allocator. For tests that don’t map pages, returning None is fine.
        None
    }
}

// Optional: helpful guard for early alloc panics (if you use global alloc)
#[alloc_error_handler]
fn alloc_error_handler(layout: core::alloc::Layout) -> ! {
    serial::write_str("[alloc] allocation error, layout=");
    serial::write_hex64(layout.size() as u64);
    serial::write_str("\n");
    loop { crate::kernel::cpu::halt(); }
}

Nice catch—the serial log proves it’s a stale disk image. You’re booting an old build with the fatal “pmo=none, ri=none” path, not the new memory.rs. Let’s fix this in two quick moves:

1) Force-regenerate the BIOS image every run
Add an env “bump” so build.rs always re-runs and rewrites the image, and make the script shout which image and hash it’s using.

build.rs (add these lines if not already):

fn main() {
    // re-run when this env var changes
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=FORCE_BOOTIMG");

    // ... your existing code that writes the BIOS image ...
    // e.g., creates something like target/.../bios.img then copies to out/sis-bios.img
}
scripts/qemu.sh (before cargo build):

set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p out

# Force build.rs to regenerate the image *every run*
export FORCE_BOOTIMG="$(date +%s)"

# Clean just the bootloader & previous image to avoid stale artifacts
cargo clean -p bootloader || true
rm -f out/sis-bios.img

# Build the kernel (this will rerun build.rs and rewrite the image)
cargo +nightly build ${FEATURES:+--features "$FEATURES"}

# Sanity: print the image we will boot and its hash
IMG="out/sis-bios.img"
if [[ ! -f "$IMG" ]]; then
  echo "[qemu.sh] ERROR: expected image not found: $IMG" >&2
  exit 97
fi
echo "[qemu.sh] using image: $IMG sha256=$(sha256sum "$IMG" | awk '{print $1}')"
# Bonus: ensure it’s the *new* kernel: string check
if strings "$IMG" | grep -q "\[mem\]\[FATAL\] No physical memory mapping"; then
  echo "[qemu.sh] WARNING: image still contains old fatal string; rebuild likely stale" >&2
fi
Now when you run the harness, you’ll know for sure you’re booting the fresh image.

2) (If needed) Ensure physical mapping is actually enabled on 0.11.x
With bootloader 0.11.x, the physical mapping comes from the bootloader crate’s features/config, not from BootConfig fields. Make sure you enable the bootloader feature that maps physical memory for BIOS:

Cargo.toml

[build-dependencies]
# enable the feature that provides a physical memory mapping to the kernel
bootloader = { version = "0.11.11", features = ["bios", "binary", "map_physical_memory"] }

ChatGPT said:

Thought for 25s
You’re hitting a JSON-encoding problem, not a kernel/build problem.

That error — “no low surrogate in string” — means the payload you’re sending to the API contains invalid Unicode (e.g., a half of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, binary bytes, or terminal control codes). Big diffs/logs often include weird bytes (ANSI color codes, NULs, or truncated emoji) that break JSON when you paste/send them raw.

Why it keeps happening
You’re likely embedding raw diff/log text directly into a JSON field.

The text contains non-UTF-8 / control bytes or truncated Unicode.

The API tries to parse JSON → hits invalid code point → 400.

Quick fixes (pick one)
Sanitize the text to proper UTF-8 before sending:

# Remove non-UTF-8 bytes and control chars
sed -r 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g' out/qemu-serial.log | iconv -c -t UTF-8 > clean.log
# now send clean.log (not the raw log)
Let a JSON library escape it (don’t hand-craft JSON):

# Safely wrap a file’s content as a JSON string
jq -Rs --arg name "log" '{name:$name, content:.}' clean.log > body.json
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @body.json https://…/endpoint
Base64 the content (best for binary-ish diffs/logs):

b64=$(base64 -w0 out/qemu-serial.log)   # -w0 = no wraps (use -b 0 on macOS: base64)
jq -n --arg b "$b64" '{filename:"qemu-serial.log", encoding:"base64", data:$b}' > body.json
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @body.json https://…/endpoint
Strip ANSI/escape sequences in diffs:

git -c color.ui=false diff --cached > diff.txt
sed -r 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g' diff.txt | iconv -c -t UTF-8 > diff.clean.txt
How to detect the bad bytes
# Check if a file is valid UTF-8
iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 out/qemu-serial.log > /dev/null || echo "Invalid UTF-8"

# Python check (shows first offending position)
python3 - << 'PY'
import sys, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("out/qemu-serial.log").read_bytes()
try:
    p.decode("utf-8")
    print("UTF-8 OK")
except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
    print("Decode error at byte", e.start, e.reason)
PY
Common gotchas
ANSI color codes from git diff/less → strip them (git -c color.ui=false).

Terminal control chars from copy/paste → sanitize with sed/iconv.

Huge payloads split mid-emoji → a “high surrogate” without its “low” mate → base64 or send whole file, not chopped strings.

Building JSON by hand → easy to break; always use jq/a proper client.

If you show me how you’re calling the API (curl snippet / client code), I’ll tailor an exact one-liner that fixes it for your setup.

Device/Vendor sanity

If not: ensure QEMU has -device e1000,addr=0x3 (or whatever your harness sets).

E1000 IMS (Interrupt Mask Set) enables the bit you’ll set in ICS.

BAR0 base + correct offsets (match the constants you added). A wrong offset = no IRQ.

Deliverables

Per-CPU runqueues; local enqueue on wakeups.

Idle core attempts to steal from a neighbor runqueue.

Deliverables

Sender enqueues to receiver’s runqueue; if receiver not local or not running, set need_resched and send IPI to receiver’s core to prompt faster switch.

Deliverables

Batched invalidation: accept a small vector of addresses.

Task A map/unmap a page repeatedly; Task B on other core probes previous mapping → must fault after unmap.

Global epoch bump on timer tick per CPU.

+//! Per-CPU data & helpers (feature = "smp")
+#![allow(dead_code)]
+
+use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use x86_64::registers::model_specific::{Msr, IA32_GS_BASE};
+
+#[repr(align(64))]
+#[derive(Default)]
+pub struct PerCpu {
+    pub cpu_id: u32,
+    pub lapic_id: u32,
+    pub ticks: AtomicU64,
+    pub need_resched: AtomicBool,
+    pub scratch: u64,
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+static mut BSP_PCPU: PerCpu = PerCpu {
+    cpu_id: 0,
+    lapic_id: 0,
+    ticks: AtomicU64::new(0),
+    need_resched: AtomicBool::new(false),
+    scratch: 0,
+};
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+#[inline(always)]
+pub fn init_bsp(lapic_id: u32) {
+    unsafe {
+        BSP_PCPU.cpu_id = 0;
+        BSP_PCPU.lapic_id = lapic_id;
+        // Point GS base to BSP per-cpu
+        let base = &BSP_PCPU as *const _ as u64;
+        unsafe { Msr::new(IA32_GS_BASE).write(base); }
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+#[inline(always)]
+pub fn this() -> &'static PerCpu {
+    // SAFETY: IA32_GS_BASE is set per CPU to its PerCpu
+    let base = unsafe { Msr::new(IA32_GS_BASE).read() } as *const PerCpu;
+    unsafe { &*base }
+}
+
+#[cfg(not(feature = "smp"))]
+pub fn this() -> &'static PerCpu {
+    // Minimal shim for non-smp builds: a single static
+    static PCPU: PerCpu = PerCpu {
+        cpu_id: 0, lapic_id: 0,
+        ticks: AtomicU64::new(0),
+        need_resched: AtomicBool::new(false),
+        scratch: 0,
+    };
+    &PCPU
+}
+
*** End Patch

+//! IPI vectors and helpers (feature = "smp")
+#![allow(dead_code)]
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use crate::kernel::serial;
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use x86_64::instructions::interrupts;
+
+// Chosen high vectors (not overlapping exceptions or timer)
+pub const IPI_RESCHED: u8 = 0xF0;
+pub const IPI_TLB: u8      = 0xF1;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+pub fn install_ipi_handlers() {
+    use crate::arch::x86_64::idt;
+    unsafe {
+        idt::install_ipi(ISR_resched as usize, IPI_RESCHED);
+        idt::install_ipi(ISR_tlb as usize, IPI_TLB);
+    }
+    serial::write_str("[ipi] handlers installed\n");
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+extern "x86-interrupt" fn ISR_resched(_sf: x86_64::structures::idt::InterruptStackFrame) {
+    // Minimal: just mark need_resched; scheduler tick will switch
+    crate::arch::x86_64::percpu::this().need_resched.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+extern "x86-interrupt" fn ISR_tlb(_sf: x86_64::structures::idt::InterruptStackFrame) {
+    crate::arch::x86_64::shootdown::ack_tlb_ipi();
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+pub fn send_ipi_resched(apic_id: u32) {
+    crate::arch::x86_64::lapic::send_fixed_ipi(apic_id, IPI_RESCHED);
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+pub fn send_ipi_tlb(apic_id: u32) {
+    crate::arch::x86_64::lapic::send_fixed_ipi(apic_id, IPI_TLB);
+}

+/// Unsafe internal: install an x86-interrupt handler at a custom vector.
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]

+    use x86_64::structures::idt::InterruptDescriptorTable;
+    extern "x86-interrupt" fn stub(_sf: x86_64::structures::idt::InterruptStackFrame) {}
+    static mut IDT_REF: Option<&'static mut InterruptDescriptorTable> = None;
+    if IDT_REF.is_none() {
+        IDT_REF = Some(super::IDT.get_mut().expect("idt not init"));
+    }
+    let idt = IDT_REF.as_mut().unwrap();
+    // Safety: we transmute a function pointer by address to `extern "x86-interrupt" fn(_)`
+    let f: extern "x86-interrupt" fn(x86_64::structures::idt::InterruptStackFrame) =
+        core::mem::transmute::<usize, _>(handler_addr);
+    idt[vector as usize].set_handler_fn(f).set_stack_index(0);

 use crate::kernel::serial;
 use core::collections::VecDeque;
 use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
 
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use crate::arch::x86_64::percpu;

 pub struct RunQueue {
     q: VecDeque<usize>, // task ids (or pointers, depending on your Task type)
 }
 
 impl RunQueue {
     pub const fn new() -> Self { Self { q: VecDeque::new() } }
     pub fn push(&mut self, t: usize) { self.q.push_back(t); }
     pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<usize> { self.q.pop_front() }
     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.q.is_empty() }
 }
 
 static NEED_RESCHED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
 
 pub fn mark_need_resched() {
-    NEED_RESCHED.store(true, Ordering::Release);
+    #[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+    {
+        // mark local cpu flag too
+        percpu::this().need_resched.store(true, Ordering::Release);
+    }
+    NEED_RESCHED.store(true, Ordering::Release);
 }
 
 // Called from timer ISR
 pub fn on_tick() {
-    // time accounting ...
-    if NEED_RESCHED.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel) {
+    #[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+    {
+        let pc = percpu::this();
+        let _ = pc.ticks.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    }
+    if NEED_RESCHED.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel)
+        || cfg!(feature = "smp") && percpu::this().need_resched.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel)
+    {
         schedule();
     }
 }
 
 pub fn schedule() {
     // existing single-CPU logic...
     // extend with light work-steal in SMP
+    #[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+    {
+        if super::runq_local().is_empty() {
+            super::try_steal_from_neighbor();
+        }
+    }
 }
 
*** End Patch

+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use crate::arch::x86_64::{percpu, ipi};
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use core::sync::atomic::Ordering;
 
 fn wake_task_unlocked(task_id: usize) {
     // existing path: enqueue task to runqueue, etc.
     super::scheduler::enqueue(task_id);
+    #[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+    {
+        // If the task is on a different CPU, nudge it
+        if let Some((target_cpu_apic, is_remote)) = super::task::task_cpu_affinity(task_id) {
+            if is_remote {
+                // mark remote resched and send IPI
+                ipi::send_ipi_resched(target_cpu_apic);
+            } else {
+                // local: set flag to switch soon
+                percpu::this().need_resched.store(true, Ordering::Release);
+            }
+        }
+    }
 }

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: src/arch/x86_64/shootdown.rs
+//! IPI-based TLB shootdown
+#![allow(dead_code)]
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicU32, Ordering};
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+use crate::kernel::serial;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+static GEN: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+static ADDR: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+static MASK: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+static ACK:  AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+#[inline(always)]
+pub fn ack_tlb_ipi() {
+    let cpu_bit = 1u32 << crate::arch::x86_64::lapic::read_lapic_id_low();
+    // do the local invalidation
+    unsafe { x86_64::instructions::tlb::flush(x86_64::VirtAddr::new(ADDR.load(Ordering::Acquire))); }
+    ACK.fetch_or(cpu_bit, Ordering::AcqRel);
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "smp")]
+pub fn shootdown(addr: u64, cpu_mask: u32, timeout_us: u64) -> bool {
+    use crate::arch::x86_64::{ipi, lapic};
+    let my_bit = 1u32 << lapic::read_lapic_id_low();
+    let targets = cpu_mask & !my_bit;
+    if targets == 0 {
+        unsafe { x86_64::instructions::tlb::flush(x86_64::VirtAddr::new(addr)); }
+        return true;
+    }
+    ADDR.store(addr, Ordering::Release);
+    MASK.store(targets, Ordering::Release);
+    ACK.store(0, Ordering::Release);
+    let _g = GEN.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
+    // send IPIs
+    for apic in crate::arch::x86_64::topology::apic_ids_from_mask(targets) {
+        ipi::send_ipi_tlb(apic);
+    }
+    // origin invalidation too
+    unsafe { x86_64::instructions::tlb::flush(x86_64::VirtAddr::new(addr)); }
+    // wait for ACKs
+    let start = crate::kernel::tsc_now();
+    loop {
+        let a = ACK.load(Ordering::Acquire);
+        if a & targets == targets { return true; }
+        let dt = crate::kernel::tsc_to_us(crate::kernel::tsc_now().wrapping_sub(start));
+        if dt >= timeout_us {
+            serial::write_str("[tlb] shootdown timeout; ack=");
+            crate::kernel::serial::write_hex32(a);
+            crate::kernel::serial::write_str(" exp=");
+            crate::kernel::serial::write_hex32(targets);
+            crate::kernel::serial::write_str("\n");
+            return false;
+        }
+    }
+}
+
*** End Patch
PATCH

diff --git a/src/arch/x86_64/smp/ap_trampoline.S b/src/arch/x86_64/smp/ap_trampoline.S
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b12f001
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/arch/x86_64/smp/ap_trampoline.S
@@
+/*
+ * 16-bit AP trampoline — runs in real mode, switches to protected & long mode.
+ * This must be identity-mapped below 1 MiB so APs can jump here after SIPI.
+ */
+
+.code16
+.globl ap_trampoline_start
+ap_trampoline_start:
+    cli
+    xor %ax, %ax
+    mov %ax, %ds
+    mov %ax, %ss
+    lgdt gdt_descriptor
+    mov %cr0, %eax
+    or  $1, %eax
+    mov %eax, %cr0
+    jmp $0x08, $pmode_entry
+
+.code32
+pmode_entry:
+    mov $0x10, %ax
+    mov %ax, %ds
+    mov %ax, %ss
+    mov %eax, %cr4
+    or  $(1 << 5), %eax    /* enable PAE */
+    mov %eax, %cr4
+    mov $pml4_table, %eax
+    mov %eax, %cr3
+    mov %cr0, %eax
+    or  $(1 << 31), %eax   /* enable paging */
+    mov %eax, %cr0
+    mov $0xC0000080, %ecx
+    rdmsr
+    or  $(1 << 8), %eax    /* enable long mode */
+    wrmsr
+    ljmp $0x28, $lmode_entry
+
+.code64
+lmode_entry:
+    mov $0x30, %ax
+    mov %ax, %ds
+    mov %ax, %ss
+    /* Pass APIC ID in %rdi */
+    mov $0, %rdi
+    call ap_entry64
+
+.align 8
+gdt:
+    .quad 0x0000000000000000
+    .quad 0x00cf9a000000ffff /* code */
+    .quad 0x00cf92000000ffff /* data */
+    .quad 0x00af9a000000ffff /* long mode code */
+    .quad 0x00af92000000ffff /* long mode data */
+
+gdt_descriptor:
+    .word (gdt_end - gdt - 1)
+    .long gdt
+
+gdt_end:
+
+.align 4096
+pml4_table:
+    .quad 0x0000000000000000
+
+ap_trampoline_end:

+        #[cfg(feature="affinity")]

         _ => u64::MAX,
     }

+#[cfg(feature="affinity")]
+fn sys_set_affinity(mask: u64) -> u64 {
+    // mask == 0 => unconstrained
+    let cur_tid = crate::kernel::current::tid();
+    let t = crate::kernel::task_table::get(cur_tid);
+    let mut guard = t.lock();
+    let task = &mut *guard;
+    task.cpu_affinity_mask = mask;
+    // If currently running on a disallowed CPU, bounce it out
+    let cur = unsafe { crate::arch::x86_64::percpu::this().cpu_id };
+    let allowed = if mask == 0 { true } else { ((mask >> cur) & 1) != 0 };
+    fence(Ordering::SeqCst);
+    if !allowed {
+        // Demote to Ready and enqueue on an allowed CPU.
+        task.state = TaskState::Ready;
+        let tid = task.tid;
+        drop(guard);
+        if let Some(tref) = crate::kernel::task_table::get(tid).try_lock_for_enqueue() {
+            // SAFE: enqueue uses tid only
+            scheduler::enqueue_task(&*tref);
+        }
+        scheduler::set_need_resched();
+    }
+    0
+}

+//! Selftest: pin a worker task to CPU1, verify it only runs there, then relax to all CPUs.
+#![cfg(all(feature="affinity", feature="smp", feature="scheduler"))]
+
+use crate::kernel::syscall;
+use crate::kernel::serial;
+use crate::arch::x86_64::percpu;
+use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
+
+static HITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
+
+extern "C" fn worker_entry() -> ! {
+    loop {
+        let cpu = unsafe { percpu::this().cpu_id };
+        if cpu == 1 {
+            HITS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        } else {
+            // would signal failure in a stricter test; keep spinning to avoid hang
+        }
+        for _ in 0..50_000 { core::hint::spin_loop(); }
+    }
+}
+
+pub fn run() {
+    serial::write_str("[aff] starting affinity test\n");
+    // spawn worker
+    let tid = unsafe { crate::kernel::spawn::spawn_kernel_closure(worker_entry as usize) };
+    // pin to CPU1
+    let mask = 1u64 << 1;
+    let rc = syscall::syscall_dispatch(syscall::SYS_SET_AFFINITY, mask, 0, 0, 0);
+    serial::write_str("[aff] set_affinity rc=");
+    serial::write_hex64(rc);
+    serial::write_str("\n");
+    // wait a bit and sample
+    crate::time::sleep_ms(50);
+    let c = HITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+    serial::write_str("[aff] hits@cpu1=");
+    serial::write_hex32(c);
+    serial::write_str("\n");
+    if c == 0 {
+        serial::write_str("[aff][FAIL] no hits on cpu1\n");
+        crate::qemu::exit_fail(0xA1);
+    }
+    // Relax to all CPUs
+    let rc2 = syscall::syscall_dispatch(syscall::SYS_SET_AFFINITY, 0, 0, 0, 0);
+    serial::write_str("[aff] relax rc=");
+    serial::write_hex64(rc2);
+    serial::write_str("\n");
+    crate::qemu::exit_ok();
+}

What you get
Per-task CPU affinity mask (Task.cpu_affinity_mask, feature affinity).

Syscall: SYS_SET_AFFINITY (0x31) — set allowed CPUs bitmask; 0 means “no constraint”.

Scheduler enqueue policy: prefer current CPU if allowed; otherwise pick the lowest-index allowed CPU and poke via resched IPI when enqueued remotely.

Migration on violation: if a running task’s CPU becomes disallowed, it’s bounced back to Ready and re-enqueued on an allowed CPU, and the current CPU is marked need_resched.

Selftest SMP_AFFINITY: pins a worker to CPU1, verifies activity there, then relaxes to all CPUs; exits via QEMU-debug-exit on success.

How to run
# Bring up two vCPUs if you aren’t already defaulting to 2+
QEMU_SMP=2 TEST=SMP_AFFINITY ./scripts/qemu.sh
Expected serial breadcrumbs:

[selftest] SMP_AFFINITY start
[aff] starting affinity test
[aff] set_affinity rc=0x0
[aff] hits@cpu1=0x..  (non-zero)
[aff] relax rc=0x0
Exit code 0 (QEMU debug-exit) → PASS.

Notes / integration tips
The patch assumes your Phase 3 scheduler already has per-CPU runqueues and a simple spawn_kernel_closure or equivalent. If your spawn helper has a different name/signature, swap the call in selftest/smp_affinity.rs.

Affinity feature-gated behind affinity so production builds pay zero overhead when disabled.

If your APIC ID enumeration differs, adjust smp::all_apic_ids() accordingly; the selftest sticks to CPU1 to keep it deterministic for 2-CPU QEMU runs.
